question: Why is the first digital image scanned into a computer only a small head of a baby?
answer: Because the machine could hold no more. In 1957 Russell Kirsch at the US National Bureau of Standards fed a photograph of his three-month-old son into a drum scanner linked to SEAC, an early stored-program computer. It could handle an array of 176 by 176 pixels, so the picture was cropped to the face.
move: Early versions of a technology are shaped by what the machine could hold.
